title: Advanced Workshop: Mastering AI Observability — Doug Guthrie, Braintrust
talk_summary: A Braintrust solutions engineer demos their evals+observability platform: tracing, code/LLM-judge scores, online scoring automations, and a 'Topics' pipeline that clusters production traces into labeled facets to surface unknown-unknown failure modes. The most transferable idea is a closed 'flywheel': production traces → automated signal → a coding agent (via CLI + skills) that queries traces with SQL, curates failing examples into datasets, writes new scores, runs evals, and opens a PR.

takeaways.technique: Production-trace flywheel into datasets and scores
takeaways.what_they_do: Curate failing/edge-case traces from production into the eval dataset, add a new score for the newly discovered failure mode, rerun evals to check improvement vs regression before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the where you start to improve the quality the most is is when you can curate traces, curate examples from production, and bring those back to your your data set

takeaways.technique: Code-based scores first, LLM judge only for subjective
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer cheap deterministic checks (schema valid, tool A called before tool B, required tools called) and reserve LLM judges for subjective quality; calibrate judges with human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code-based score. These are generally uh very fast, very cheap, uh and very easy to run... was tool A called before tool B?

takeaways.what_they_do: Use binary pass/fail rather than graded scales early on, write deliberately hard cases, and treat perfect scores as a sign the test set or rubric is too weak.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you get 100% on every single one of your evals... you probably don't have uh strong enough test cases

takeaways.technique: Cheap clustering pass over 100% of traces instead of LLM-judging all
takeaways.what_they_do: A preprocessor summarizes each trace, a cheap hosted model labels facets, embeddings cluster them into a topic map so you get signal on all traffic at low cost; sampling rate scales down as agent matures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 6 cents per um, million tokens on the input side and 40 cents on the output side
takeaways.numbers: ~$0.06/M input, $0.40/M output tokens for the topics pipeline

takeaways.technique: CLI + skill so coding agents drive the observability loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose trace data via a CLI that supports arbitrary SQL, and install a 'skill' so the coding agent can query traces, view spans, create datasets/scores, run evals, and open a PR autonomously.
takeaways.evidence_quote: give your coding agents the ability to run that automated flywheel... I want it to view traces. I want it to view spans. I want it to create new scores and run evals
takeaways.numbers: one customer generates 5-10 more PRs per day

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach scoring/analysis to a specific span, a whole trace, or a group keyed by a shared ID (e.g. conversation ID) so multi-turn/long-running work is evaluated as a unit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have that multi-turn conversation that exists across multiple traces, you would use this group and then use that sort of common um identifier
